A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreeKV and contain complete, readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Each has 12 pages ending with references; neither contains an appendix. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy experiments in Tables 2–3, latency measurements in Figure 7, and efficiency ablations in Figure 8.

after.justification: v2 retains the original accuracy experiments in Tables 2–3, latency measurements in Figure 7, and efficiency ablations in Figure 8.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain identical speculative retrieval, group-consistent selection, fine-grained correction, hybrid KV layouts, and double-buffered streamed recall procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LongBench v2, LongGenBench, MATH500, AIME24, and GPQA. The introductory NIAH/summarization comparisons and long-input/long-generation efficiency scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain full-KV references and RazorAttention, RaaS, Quest, ArkVale, and ShadowKV. Figure 7 retains the same four efficiency comparators: ArkVale, ShadowKV, RaaS, and RazorAttention.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains identical models, baseline adaptations, metrics, sampling procedures, and budgets, including a 2048-token retrieval budget, page size 32, 64K input truncation for LongBench v2, and 16K generation limits.

E4.justification: Figure 3 retains the same query-similarity and attention-pattern analyses. Figure 8 retains identical ablations of hybrid layouts, double buffering, and speculative retrieval; no supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report k=8 sampled answers per reasoning problem with pass@k and avg@k in Section 5.2. Repeated-sampling and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and findings in Tables 2–3 and the empirical figures are unchanged. For example, FreeKV's Llama-3.1-8B LongBench v2 overall accuracy remains 29.22, and Figure 7 retains the maximum 13.74× speedup over ArkVale.

T1.justification: The attention and retrieval definitions in Section 2.1 and the similarity, selection, and correction mathematics in Section 3 are identical. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same algorithm-system contributions and claims of near-lossless accuracy with up to 13× speedup over existing KV retrieval methods.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of baseline accuracy and efficiency, and Section 6 discussion are unchanged, including the qualification about page-wise selection at small budgets.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures are identical, including task-specific thresholds, baseline modifications, tensor layouts, and the A100 40GB GPU with AMD 7302 CPUs connected through PCIe Gen4.

R1.justification: The same 49 references and related-work comparisons are retained. The paper's positioning relative to KV dropping and retrieval methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes Jing Lin, Yiwu Yao, and Danning Ke from the author list and removes the Huawei affiliation and numerical affiliation markers. It updates the arXiv version/date stamp and changes one occurrence of 'SoTA' to 'SOTA'; scientific prose and section structure otherwise match.

P2.justification: The shortened author block occupies one author line instead of two, shifting the abstract and introduction slightly upward on page 1. All figures and tables retain identical content, styling, and placement; rendered pages 3–12 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: The methods, experimental evidence, claims, and discussion are unchanged. The author/affiliation revisions, version stamp update, capitalization edit, and minor first-page reflow provide no evidence of a meaningful net improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
